serving_utility: Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW; TVA wholesale)
load_basis: Trade-press report (CRE Daily, 2025-09-19) of capacity live at the site in Sept 2025, self-generated rather than grid-delivered; a year-end 2025 figure was not found and is likely higher
notes: KEY CORRECTION: the territory utility is right (MLGW = City of Memphis), but the computing load is NOT on MLGW's system. MLGW statement dated 2025-07-22: its general services agreement at 5420 Tulane Road 'is supplying around .5 MW' and 'MLGW is not supplying power to their supercomputer, Colossus 2.' MLGW's 2025 xAI Update (https://www.mlgw.com/images/content/files/pdf/new/xAI%202025%20Update.pdf) adds that xAI had not submitted a final electric request for Tulane Road, so no system impact study was under way. The site runs on gas turbines (CRE Daily: former power-plant site in Southaven, MS, about 6 miles away, running seven turbines) and batteries. Canary Media, 2026-09-11 (https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/batteries/xai-massive-battery-memphis-data-center), still describes temporary gas generators for Colossus 2 and a TVA board approval on 2026-08-20 of a direct grid hookup for the battery. So our 946 MW should not be counted as MLGW retail load in 2025; only about 0.5 MW was. Year: CRE Daily says the building was bought in March 2025 and 200 MW was live six months later; MLGW's July 2025 statement already refers to the supercomputer. Planned: 1,100 MW is the grid amount MLGW said xAI had discussed for Tulane Road (Daily Memphian, 2025-05-06, https://dailymemphian.com/article/51712/xai-second-datacenter-could-use-enough-electricity-to-power-40-percent-of-memphis), described as not formally studied; CRE Daily reports 'over 1 gigawatt' planned and E&E News (2025-05-09) reports up to 1.56 GW of turbines under consideration. A TVA approval of an additional 150 MW for xAI as an MLGW customer was reported 2026-02-12 (WSMV) without naming the site. The worklist point sits on the TN/MS line; West Memphis (AR) is not relevant. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

site_name: QTS Richmond campus (former Qimonda fab), 6000 Technology Blvd, Sandston
serving_utility: Dominion Energy Virginia (Virginia Electric and Power Co)
notes: Utility: Data Center Frontier (2017-05-10) describes 'the 110 megawatt substation from Dominion Virginia Power' on the campus. Tariff versus special contract not verified. Year: Data Center Knowledge (2010-11-03) reports QTS opened the campus that week and the first 50,000 sq ft phase 'came online Monday'; QTS bought the former chip fab out of bankruptcy in 2010. Our 2001 guess reflects generators permitted for the fab, not data-center operation. Load: QTS's own site page (https://qtsdatacenters.com/data-centers/richmond/, which redirects to q.com) lists '238 MW' as critical campus capacity for a master-planned six-facility campus but does not say how much is built or loaded, so it is recorded as planned capacity and load_mw_2025 is left null. Earlier figures: 100 MW campus power capacity (DCK 2010), 110 MW Dominion substation (DCF 2017). Our 257.7 MW is close to the operator's campus capacity, not a verified 2025 load. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

site_name: Microsoft MWH Data Center (formerly Oxford), 1515 Port Industrial Parkway, Quincy
serving_utility: Grant County PUD (Public Utility District No. 2 of Grant County)
notes: Utility: Basin Business Journal (2022-05-10) quotes the head of Grant PUD's large power solutions team naming 'the massive Microsoft campus in Quincy' among the county's largest power users, in an article on PUD supply to Quincy. It does not name this address, and no PUD document naming the MWH site was found, hence medium. Rate schedule not verified. Year: Ecology Approval Order 22AQ-E035 (2022-09-27) calls MWH 'an existing data center' and lists MWH01 generator commission dates of 2015-09-21 and 2015-11-13, with later buildings commissioned 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022. First commercial operation is therefore late 2015 or early 2016; no operator statement of the opening date was found. Our 2023 guess is wrong: the 2022 permit only added renewable diesel as a fuel at an existing site. The original approval (14AQ-E537) dates to August 2014 and the MWH03-06 expansion (72 more generators) to order 18AQ-E024 in 2018 (https://ecology.wa.gov/getattachment/8ec0689d-1913-4cda-ae96-428b23f63d04/20181023MWH_TSD.pdf). Load: no public figure for this site. Context only: Grant PUD says its 8 data-center operators together averaged about 280 aMW in 2025 (https://www.grantpud.org/blog/data-center-faqs, 2026-08-28), so our 208.8 MW for this one campus looks high as an average load. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

site_name: AWS Hilliard campus (permit name CMH052), 5109 Hayden Run Rd, Hilliard
notes: Utility: joint application of Amazon Data Services and Ohio Power Company, PUCO Case No. 23-0858-EL-AEC (public redacted version, copy hosted by NBC4): ADS operates data centers 'in AEP Ohio's territory' on campuses 'in Hilliard, Dublin, and New Albany.' The City of Columbus municipal utility is not the provider. Arrangement changed over time: the existing campuses were under a PUCO-approved economic development arrangement from 2018 (Case No. 17-1827-EL-AEC), which ADS exited effective 2023-05-31 once those campuses were built out (footnote 3 of the application); the 2023 arrangement covers new campuses only. Recorded as retail for 2025; treat 2018 to May 2023 as special contract. Year: Data Center Knowledge (2017-11-15) says the Dublin, Hilliard and New Albany facilities 'came online about one year ago,' i.e. 2016. That this address is the original 2016 Hilliard campus rests on a directory lead, not a cited source, and the 2021 generator permit suggests CMH052 itself may be a later building on the campus, hence medium. MW figures are redacted in the PUCO filing; no public load figure found, our 147.2 MW is unverified. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

site_name: Google Lancaster data center, Whiley Road, Lancaster
load_basis: Utility-projected site demand, not metered load: AEP's PJM supplemental need AEP-2023-OH078 (Appendix B of the OPSB filing) gives 96 MW of incremental demand for the second phase, 'bringing the total load for the customer's site to 196 MW,' with a requested in-service date of 2024-09-30
notes: Our guess (South Central Power) is wrong on the evidence found. Ohio Power Company's Construction Notice for the Sifford-Ruble 2 138 kV Tie-Lines (OPSB Case No. 24-2384-EL-BNR, 2024-04-10) describes two more tie-lines from the Company's Sifford Station to 'the customer's stepdown substation (Ruble Station)' on customer property at about 105 Whiley Road, Lancaster, lat 39.727034, lon -82.691825, which matches our point (39.72703, -82.68311). The filing does not name the customer, so the link to Google rests on location, the two-phase build and the scale; hence medium rather than high. It also says the Company 'filed and in-serviced' the first Sifford-Ruble tie lines (Case No. 22-0153-EL-BNR) 'to serve the initial customer request,' and Sifford Station was approved in Case No. 21-0860-EL-BLN. Tariff versus special contract not verified. Year: not pinned. AP reported on 2023-05-03 that the Lancaster data center would be built, and by April 2024 AEP called the customer 'existing' with initial service in place, so first operation falls between mid-2023 and early 2024; no source gives the date, so the field is null (our 2024 guess is plausible but unverified). Load: 196 MW is the utility's projected total (100 MW initial plus 96 MW phase two, tie-lines expected in service October 2024); our 137 MW is not contradicted as an actual 2025 load. Google holds expansion land but no full-buildout figure was found. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

site_name: AWS Umatilla campus, 80939 Powerline Road, Umatilla
notes: Our guess (PacifiCorp) is wrong on the evidence found. Amazon's own article (2023-04-04) calls Umatilla Electric Cooperative (UEC) 'the electric cooperative serving AWS in Umatilla and Morrow Counties' and a 'provider of reliable utility service to AWS data centers in UEC's service territory.' That statement is county-wide and does not name this address, hence medium; no UEC or permit document naming the Powerline Road site was found. UEC's projects page (https://www.umatillaelectric.com/about-us/news-events-updates/projects/) lists recent 230 kV and substation work in and around the city of Umatilla (Rockpile line, McNary to Wanapa line, Basalt Substation at the Port of Umatilla) without naming customers. BPA is UEC's wholesale and transmission supplier, not the retail provider. The Oregonian (2023-04-11, via https://lagrandeobserver.com/?p=154421) reports Amazon working with UEC to choose its own electricity supply, so a customer-specific supply arrangement is possible but not verified. Year and load: no acceptable source found; directory sites give dates and per-building MW but are not citable under the rules. Our 2023 year (from a 2022 generator permit) and 85.5 MW are unverified. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.

Our 2024 guess reflects a 2023 generator permit for one of at least five expansions (2011, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 per Area Development), not first operation. No public MW figure found; our 79.1 MW is unverified and probably covers one building rather than the campus. site_name: Switch Pyramid campus (Grand Rapids), 6100 E Paris Ave SE, Gaines Township
notes: Our guess (DTE Electric) is wrong; Consumers Energy was one of the other mapped candidates. A May 2017 Site Selection investment profile prepared under the auspices of Consumers Energy and hosted on consumersenergy.com describes the utility's work to power the former Steelcase Pyramid for Switch in Gaines Township, Kent County, quoting Switch asking Consumers whether it could 'provide enough power to this data center' and Consumers answering yes to that and to a 100 percent renewable option. Whether service is under a standard tariff, a renewable program or a special contract was not verified. Year: the same profile says 'The 225,000-sq.-ft. first phase went on line last June,' i.e. June 2016; Switch's own announcement that the campus was 'now open' came in early 2017 (https://switch.com/?p=3977), so 2017 is the alternative reading, hence medium. Our 2024 guess reflects a 2023 generator permit for a later expansion. Planned: Switch states the campus is designed for 'up to 320 megawatts (MW) of power' (switch.com); the Consumers profile gives 200 MW. No public figure for 2025 operating load; our 67.4 MW is unverified. Lat/lon left null per the output spec; county from the FCC census-area lookup on the worklist point.
